chunks.heading: HDF5 from Fortran
chunks.text:
Facts about using HDF5 from Fortran that cause wrong data, unreadable files or failed builds. "Measured" means
observed with HDF5 2.0.0 (a parallel build with the Fortran interface, built with gfortran 14.2) on Linux.

chunks.heading: HDF5 from Fortran > Call h5open_f before anything else
chunks.text:
The Fortran predefined type identifiers (`H5T_NATIVE_DOUBLE`, `H5T_NATIVE_INTEGER`, ...) are variables of the
`hdf5` module set by `h5open_f`. Before it they hold 0 (measured: `H5T_NATIVE_DOUBLE` printed 0 before
`h5open_f` and a large identifier after), so a call made earlier passes an invalid identifier to the library.
Call `h5open_f` once at start-up and `h5close_f` at the end.

chunks.heading: HDF5 from Fortran > Dimensions appear reversed
chunks.text:
HDF5 stores dataspaces in C (row-major) order. A Fortran array `rho(3, 2)` written with dimensions `[3, 2]`
appears as `( 2, 3 )` in `h5dump` (measured); the values are in the file in Fortran memory order, so element
`rho(i, j)` is `[j-1][i-1]` on the C side. Tools written in C or Python (h5py) see the transpose. FoBiS's
`hdf5` probe reports the stored (C-order) shape, and `fobis verify` labels the worst element of such a
quantity with 0-based C indices.

chunks.heading: HDF5 from Fortran > The Fortran module belongs to one compiler
chunks.text:
`use hdf5` reads the `hdf5.mod` of the installation, which only the compiler that built HDF5 can read (module
formats differ between compilers and between gfortran releases: compilers pack). Keep one HDF5 build per
compiler, and select it together with the compiler (a module system, or `ext_libs`/`include` per fobos mode).
The `h5fc` wrapper (`h5pfc` for parallel HDF5) prints the flags it adds with `h5fc -show`; the build settings
are in `lib/libhdf5.settings` of the installation (`Fortran: ON`, `Parallel HDF5: ON`).

chunks.heading: HDF5 from Fortran > Parallel HDF5
chunks.text:
A parallel build (`Parallel HDF5: ON` in `libhdf5.settings`) needs MPI at compile and link time: use the
`h5pfc` wrapper or the MPI wrapper with the HDF5 flags, and open files with an MPI-IO file access property list
(`h5pset_fapl_mpio_f`). Collective operations, and transfers set to collective with `h5pset_dxpl_mpio_f`, must be
called by every rank of the communicator, including ranks that write no data (with an empty selection); a rank
that skips the call makes the others wait.

chunks.heading: HDF5 from Fortran > File locking
chunks.text:
HDF5 locks every file it opens (since release 1.10). On file systems where the lock fails, the open fails or a
reader gets nothing; the maintainer observed Windows ParaView reading an XDMF/HDF5 dataset from a WSL share
(`\\wsl$\...`) as empty, without an error. Setting `HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING=FALSE` in the reader's environment
disables locking: safe for read-only viewing, unsafe when several processes write the same file. The measured
build reports `Use file locking: best-effort` in its settings (lock failures ignored where the file system does
not support locks).

chunks.heading: HDF5 from Fortran > Reading HDF5 in FoBiS cases
chunks.text:
A case quantity `name : hdf5 FILE /group/dataset` is read with h5py when it is importable, else with the
`h5dump` command; when neither is available the quantity is reported as not read, with the reason, instead of
failing silently. Load the HDF5 tools (for example with the module that provides them) before
`fobis case run` or `fobis verify`.

chunks.heading: MPI implementations: Open MPI, Intel MPI, MPICH family
chunks.text:
What differs between MPI implementations in practice: launchers, environment, compiler wrappers, Fortran
modules. The semantics of MPI itself are in the mpi pack. "Measured" means observed with Open MPI 5.0.7 (built
with gfortran 14.2) and Intel MPI 2021.18 on one Linux machine with 16 processors.

chunks.heading: MPI implementations: Open MPI, Intel MPI, MPICH family > Identify the implementation
chunks.text:
`mpirun --version` prints `mpirun (Open MPI) 5.0.7` or `Intel(R) MPI Library for Linux* OS, Version 2021.18.1
...` (measured); MPICH prints a `HYDRA build details` block. `fobis case run` and `fobis verify` record this line
in the provenance of every case run with ranks.

chunks.heading: MPI implementations: Open MPI, Intel MPI, MPICH family > More ranks than processors
chunks.text:
Open MPI refuses to start more processes than there are slots (processors detected, without a hostfile or a
batch allocation). Measured, `mpirun -np 17` on 16 processors:

```
There are not enough slots available in the system to satisfy the 17
slots that were requested by the application:
```

`mpirun --oversubscribe -np 17` runs them. Intel MPI started 17 processes on the same machine without a flag
(measured). Oversubscribed ranks share cores, so their timings say nothing about the code. For FoBiS cases set
the launcher in the fobos, for example `[verification] launcher = mpirun --oversubscribe -np {ranks}`.

chunks.heading: MPI implementations: Open MPI, Intel MPI, MPICH family > Rank and size in the environment
chunks.text:
Each launcher tells the processes who they are through environment variables, readable before `MPI_Init`
(for example to choose a GPU per rank). Measured:

| Implementation | rank | size | rank on the node |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open MPI 5 | `OMPI_COMM_WORLD_RANK` (also `PMIX_RANK`) | `OMPI_COMM_WORLD_SIZE` | `OMPI_COMM_WORLD_LOCAL_RANK` |
| Intel MPI | `PMI_RANK` | `PMI_SIZE` | `MPI_LOCALRANKID` |

Under Slurm's `srun` the variables are `SLURM_PROCID`, `SLURM_NTASKS` and `SLURM_LOCALID` (Slurm
documentation). Code that reads one implementation's variables silently gets nothing under another: read them
with a fallback, or use `MPI_Comm_split_type` with `MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED` after `MPI_Init` for the node-local
rank.

chunks.heading: MPI implementations: Open MPI, Intel MPI, MPICH family > Compiler wrappers
chunks.text:
`mpif90`/`mpifort` call a Fortran compiler with the MPI include and library flags. Which compiler is not fixed
by the name:

- Open MPI: the compiler it was built with; `mpif90 --showme` prints the command (measured:
  `gfortran -I... -lmpi_usempif08 -lmpi_usempi_ignore_tkr -lmpi_mpifh -lmpi`).
- Intel MPI: `mpif90 -show` printed a gfortran command (with modules for gfortran 15.1 under
  `include/mpi/gfortran/15.1.0`), while `mpiifx -show` printed an ifx command (measured).

FoBiS modes with `mpi = True` compile with `mpif90` for gnu and nvfortran, `mpiifort` for `intel` and
`mpiifort -fc=ifx` for `intel_nextgen`; `fobis introspect --compiler` shows the command a mode runs. With Intel
MPI's `mpif90` a gnu mode gets gfortran, as intended; check the wrapper whenever several MPI installations are
on the PATH.

chunks.heading: MPI implementations: Open MPI, Intel MPI, MPICH family > Fortran modules belong to one compiler
chunks.text:
The `mpi` and `mpi_f08` modules are compiled `.mod` files: they work only with the compiler (and module format)
that built them. Measured with an Open MPI built by gfortran 14.2: ifx stops with `error #7013: This module file
was not generated by any release of this compiler`, nvfortran with `NVFORTRAN-F-0004-Corrupt or Old Module
file`. Each compiler needs its own MPI build (or, for Intel MPI, its own module directory). The legacy
`include 'mpif.h'` avoids the module but loses argument checking, and is deprecated (mpi pack).

chunks.heading: MPI implementations: Open MPI, Intel MPI, MPICH family > GPU-aware MPI
chunks.text:
Passing device buffers directly to MPI calls needs an MPI built with GPU support. For Open MPI:

```
ompi_info --parsable --all | grep opal_built_with_cuda_support:value
```

prints `...:value:false` for a build without it (measured). Without GPU support, a device address passed to MPI
is read as a host address: a crash or wrong data. With OpenACC, use `!$acc host_data use_device(buf)` only
when the MPI is GPU-aware; otherwise update the host copy before the call (hpc-practice pack).
